_comment: What one Performance+ probe measurement must record for it to count.
The G0 gate exists because Worker vs Window, the transport, the frame
clock and the WebView host shape are unresolved, and a design that picks
one without device evidence has picked it by preference. This file is the
other half of that discipline: it says what evidence looks like, so a run
cannot be accepted because it was the only one anybody did.
Two rules shape every required field below:
1. A MISSING FIELD REJECTS THE RUN, not the record. A record that lost
its thermal state is not a slightly worse sample; it is a sample
nobody can tell apart from one taken on a hot phone, and averaging it
in is how a thermally-throttled arm wins.
2. EVERY DIMENSION IS RECORDED EVEN WHEN IT IS NOT THE VARIABLE. A run
that varies transport still records agent, clock and layout, because
'one variable at a time' can only be checked against records that say
what all the other variables were.
Enforced by tools/apple-probe-decision/decide.py. These are the
sentences from the design that would otherwise live only in prose, and
prose does not fail a build.
decision_rules._seed_comment: Fixed so a decision is reproducible from the same raw data. A tool that returns a different winner on a second run is not evidence.

primary_metric.name: input_to_present_p95_ms
primary_metric._comment: The number the lane exists to improve. Secondary metrics are recorded and reported but never override it.

_enum_comment: The enums are closed on purpose. An unrecognised value is a run that
measured something this decision cannot name, and silently bucketing it
with the nearest known value is how a hybrid transport's numbers end up

variables._comment: The four G0 choices. A decision may be made for one of these only when the matrix isolates it.
variables.agent: Window versus Dedicated Worker. Note that Window cannot serve synchronous content at all, so a Window win is an admission rule, never a replacement of the default.
variables.transport: Loopback WebSocket versus a custom-scheme binary request path.
variables.clock: Worker rAF where feature detection finds it, Window rAF relayed, or a host CADisplayLink relayed.
